newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's president sees poll in May or June.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's president sees poll in May or June.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual on Tuesday proposed May 29 or June 5, 1997, as tentative dates for his country's multiparty parliamentary elections, Algerian state-radio said.

Zeroual also pledged that the elections would be held freely without any pressure exerted on voters, said the radio quoting Talbi Mohamed Cherif, leader of Development and Solidarity National Party (PNSD).
Mohamed Cherif was one of 10 political party leaders who met Zeroual on Tuesday to discuss preparations for parliamentary elections.
PNSD is a small moderate party supporting government attempts to pull Algeria out of a five-year civil strife through elections while pursuing an iron-fist policy to try and quash Moslem guerrillas.

Main secular opposition group stayed away from the talks, saying Algeria needs peace before holding any elections. The Socialist Forces Front (FFS) argues that two polls in 1995 and 1996 led only to escalating violence.

FFS has urged authorities since 1992 to open negotiations with the main opposition parties, including the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front -- which was banned after the 1992 polls were cancelled -- to end the bloodshed before holding elections. More than 60,000 people have died since Moslem rebels took up arms in 1992 after the polls were cancelled.

Officials and party sources told Reuters by telephone from Algiers that an independent committee to supervise the elections planned for the first half of this year was the main topic on the meeting's agenda.
They added later that other items, including the worsening security situation, were also addressed because politicians were wary about possible low voter participation due to the continuing violence.
"The president assured us the elections will take place in a climate free of violence," said Mohamed Cherif summing up the talks with Zeroual.
